items.stem: Which one of the following statements about population growth and the demographic transition theory is correct?
items.answer: In the second stage of the demographic transition, fertility remains high in the beginning while mortality falls.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: It grows fastest in the second stage, when mortality falls but fertility is still high. Natural growth is births minus deaths only; actual growth also includes migration. Both are high in the first stage.
options: In the first stage of the demographic transition, both fertility and mortality are low.
Population always grows fastest in the last stage of the demographic transition.
In the second stage of the demographic transition, fertility remains high in the beginning while mortality falls.
Natural growth of population includes migration.

items.stem: "River valleys such as the Ganga plains are densely populated." Examine this statement with reference to factors influencing population distribution.
items.answer: The statement is valid. They have flat land, fertile soils and water for drinking and irrigation.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (they have flat land, fertile soils and water for drinking and irrigation.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about distribution and density of world population is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Most of the ten most populous countries are in Africa."
items.answer: Six of them are located in Asia.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Six of them are located in Asia.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: The population of District A was 230,000 in 2001 and 287,500 in 2011. What was its percentage growth rate over the decade?
District E has a population of 1,700,000 on 2,500 sq km; District B has 990,000 people on 1,500 sq km. Calculate the density of population of each and state which is more densely populated.
items.answer: District E: 680 persons per sq km; District B: 660 persons per sq km; District E is more densely populated.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for each density (population ÷ area = 680 and 660 persons per sq km), 1 for the comparison (District E).

items.stem: What is meant by 'geographical factors' in the context of factors influencing population distribution?
items.answer: Physical factors such as availability of water, landforms, climate and soils that influence where people live.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: geographical factors correctly explained as physical factors such as availability of water, landforms, climate and soils that influence where people live.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about migration and population control:
I. Unemployment at the place of origin is a pull factor.
II. Family planning, by spacing or preventing births, is a measure of population control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: It is a push factor; pull factors are attractions at the destination. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following extract on migration and population control and answer the questions that follow.
"Migration may be permanent, temporary or seasonal. Family planning, by spacing or preventing births, is a measure of population control. People generally migrate for better economic and social life."
(i) Migrants who move into a new place are called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'migration' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: People migrate from rural to urban areas. (1)
items.answer: (i) immigrants (ii) The movement of people from one place to another, which changes the population of both places. (iii) Cities offer better job opportunities and living conditions, which act as pull factors.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) immigrants (ii) The movement of people from one place to another, which changes the population of both places. (iii) Cities offer better job opportunities and living conditions, which act as pull factors.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about population growth and the demographic transition theory:
I. Natural growth of population includes migration.
II. In the first stage of the demographic transition, both fertility and mortality are low.
III. Crude birth rate and crude death rate are expressed per thousand of population.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: III only
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: Natural growth is births minus deaths only; actual growth also includes migration. II is incorrect: Both are high in the first stage. III is correct.
options: I and II only
All of them
I only
III only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about distribution and density of world population is NOT correct?
items.answer: Density of population is measured as area per person.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. It is measured as the number of persons per unit area, usually per sq km.
options: Each unit of land has limited capacity to support people, so density helps to understand the balance between people and land.
About 90 per cent of the world's population lives in about 10 per cent of its land area.
Density of population is measured as area per person.
Areas such as polar regions, high mountains and hot deserts are very sparsely populated.

items.stem: In one year, a region with a population of 520,000 recorded 17,000 births, 8,000 deaths, 4,000 in-migrants and 3,000 out-migrants. Calculate (a) the natural increase and (b) the population at the end of the year. Name the three components of population change.
items.answer: (a) Natural increase = births − deaths = 9,000. (b) Population = 520,000 + 9,000 + 4,000 − 3,000 = 530,000. Components: births, deaths and migration.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for natural increase, 1 for the final population, 1 for naming births, deaths and migration.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on factors influencing population distribution and answer the questions that follow.
"Cities offer better civic amenities and job opportunities, which attract migrants from rural areas. Areas with extreme climates such as hot or cold deserts are less preferred for settlement. People prefer to live in areas where fresh water is easily available."
(i) Which type of landform is generally preferred by people for living? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'economic factors' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Cities attract people from rural areas. (1)
items.answer: (i) Flat plains and gentle slopes (ii) Factors such as minerals, industrialisation and urbanisation that attract people to an area. (iii) They offer jobs, better civic amenities and services.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Flat plains and gentle slopes (ii) Factors such as minerals, industrialisation and urbanisation that attract people to an area. (iii) They offer jobs, better civic amenities and services.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about population growth and the demographic transition theory is NOT correct?
items.answer: In the first stage of the demographic transition, both fertility and mortality are low.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Both are high in the first stage.
options: Growth of population can be positive or negative.
In the first stage of the demographic transition, both fertility and mortality are low.
In the last stage of the demographic transition, population is stable or grows slowly, and people are urbanised, literate and technologically advanced.
Crude birth rate and crude death rate are expressed per thousand of population.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Some areas of the world are densely populated while others are almost empty.
Reason (R): Areas with extreme climates such as hot or cold deserts are less preferred for settlement.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both statements are true, but R deals with a different point and does not explain A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Attractions at the destination, such as better jobs, living conditions, peace, security and pleasant climate, that draw people.
items.answer: pull factors
items.markingKey: (c) pull factors: attractions at the destination, such as better jobs, living conditions, peace, security and pleasant climate, that draw people.
options: social and cultural factors
density of population
pull factors
population distribution

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Ganga plains are among the most densely populated areas of the world because of fertile alluvial soils and flat land. Places of religious or cultural significance attract people. Areas with extreme climates such as hot or cold deserts are less preferred for settlement. Industrial belts provide job opportunities and attract large numbers of people."
(i) Explain the term 'economic factors', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: River valleys such as the Ganga plains are densely populated. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Mountains and plateaus are the most densely populated landforms." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) Factors such as minerals, industrialisation and urbanisation that attract people to an area. (ii) They have flat land, fertile soils and water for drinking and irrigation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Plains and gentle slopes are preferred; mountains are sparsely populated.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Factors such as minerals, industrialisation and urbanisation that attract people to an area. (ii) They have flat land, fertile soils and water for drinking and irrigation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Plains and gentle slopes are preferred; mountains are sparsely populated.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about migration and population control is correct?
items.answer: Migration may be permanent, temporary or seasonal.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: It changes the population of both the place of origin and the place of destination. Emigrants move out of a place; immigrants move in. It is a push factor; pull factors are attractions at the destination.
options: Unemployment at the place of origin is a pull factor.
Emigrants are people who move into a new place.
Migration may be permanent, temporary or seasonal.
Migration affects only the place of destination.

items.stem:
Statement: People migrate from rural to urban areas.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Cities offer better job opportunities and living conditions, which act as pull factors.
items.markingKey: (d) Cities offer better job opportunities and living conditions, which act as pull factors.
options: Physical, economic and social factors such as water, climate, soil, minerals, industry and urbanisation vary from place to place.
Spacing or preventing births helps to check rapid population growth.
Their extreme climate, lack of water and poor soils make it difficult for people to live there.
Cities offer better job opportunities and living conditions, which act as pull factors.
